label: D-02a44d

defects.summary: GitScratch.AfterUnlink is an AsyncLocal, and this test sets it inside the async InitializeAsync after an await, so the value never reaches the test method; S5.6.7's 'the recorder never invoked' check (_unlinked empty) is vacuous and cannot go red, while every other recorder test in the suite sets the seam inside the test method.

The 'refused' ending does not check that the row's scratch is gone, although QuestionRowLaunch makes the scratch and its copies before the launch control refuses; deviation 53 says this ending 'has no scratch to check', which is not accurate.
MustCarryNoFlags refuses Flags and Leading but not AddDirs, which are also argv flags, so a plan with --add-dir pairs passes without notice although decision 3 says a plan with ANY flag is refused.

Deviation 53 says the spec's trigger for the refused row is 'a changed slot key', but the spec names no such trigger; several items (47, 55, 58, 59, 61) are not deviations from the spec but notes on the spec or on the host.
The E5.5 tests were never seen red (the plan admits that no mutation proofs were run), and the class copies Scopes, StandIn and ArgOf from AKimiConsultationScenarioTests instead of sharing them.
The new `why` line starts in lower case ('the kimi rows cite…') and splits the earlier sentence about empty `cells` into its own line, unlike the surrounding text.
S5.6.5 checks 'no --session' only on the none build, not on the disk build, though the Then applies to both.

summary: The production change is small and matches every E5.5/E5.6 decision: the kimi planner arm with no flags, the refusal of a flagged plan, the three unconfined/unconfined/unmeasured rows with their cells, the vectors, the hand-written Runtimes list and the regenerated TS table; all 12 scenarios exist and pass, and nothing new fails. The main weakness is test honesty: S5.6.7's junction recorder is set where it never reaches the test, the E5.5 tests were never seen red, and some of the deviation entries are not quite true or are not deviations.
